name: style-newsroom
title: Newsroom wire-service style
description: A writing-style profile rather than a detector: ten document-level edges, forming six bands, that measure how closely a document sits to wire-service news writing. Four of the six are two-sided, so a document that runs far past the register in the permitted direction reports as readily as one that falls short of it; the two one-sided ceilings say in their own notes why the reference median of 0.0 leaves them nothing to put a floor on. The guidance comes from three published sources - the Reuters Handbook of Journalism (the copy linked in source; its home at handbook.reuters.com now redirects to Reuters' journalistic-standards page), the BBC News styleguide (https://www.peteburns.com/downloads/BBC%20news%20styleguide.pdf) and the Associated Press Statement of News Values and Principles (https://www.ap.org/about/news-values-and-principles/) - and every number comes from 35 news stories measured for this file, not from taste. Rates are computed only where a document reads as prose: nine of the ten rules use the engine's default gate of 4 to 60 words a sentence, and the reference stories run between 17 and 38, so the gate holds the whole register with room on either side and a file that carries markup rather than sentences does not reach them at all. The tenth, the long-sentence edge, runs a wider ceiling for the reason its own note gives. Each rule is off by default and reports a rate for the whole document rather than marking a span, so nothing here changes what any other rule set reports. The thresholds are the first thing to change: they describe agency copy in August 2026, and a newsroom with a different house style would move all of them.

corpus.note: 20 Associated Press and 15 BBC News articles of 300 words or more, taken from their front pages on 28 August 2026, body text only. Band edges are the p10 and p90 of that distribution except where a rule's measured field says otherwise. Every rule also records how often it reports on this project's local corpus of human technical documents, 16 of which reach the default prose gate and 17 the wider ceiling the long-sentence edge uses, which is not in this register and is there only to show the size of the gap. The gate on nine of the ten rules is the engine's default of 4 to 60 words a sentence, the long-sentence edge alone running to 120: the reference stories run 16.6 to 38.4, so nothing in the register is near either edge, and the documents the gate turns away are the ones where the count would be measuring markup - a file of Python source averages 80 words between one period and the next, and a page of bullet points 136.

voice: Third person, past tense, active. One idea to a sentence and the important one first. Every contested claim belongs to somebody who can be named, and the verb is said. Colour comes from the detail and the quotation, never from the adjective.

tension.note: The wikipedia-ai set reports unnamed authorities - experts say, critics argue, observers note. Raising this profile's attribution rate by adding them would trip it, correctly: the newsroom answer to both is a source with a name and a title. Findings from that set stand.

The em-dash set reports every em dash, and this repository selects it. Agency copy uses one in the dateline of every story it files. This profile has no opinion on em dashes and does not measure them; that set's findings stand. Anyone who disagrees can put em-dash in the ignore list of their own slop.json.

The humanizer-de set measures the same coefficient of variation with a ceiling at 0.4, below this profile's even edge of 0.57. They compose: between 0.4 and 0.57 only this profile reports, and below 0.4 both do and agree.
The economist candidate set reports fewer than 20 sentence endings per 1000 words. This profile's long edge is 31, so between 20 and 31 only this profile reports, and below 20 both do.

The arxiv-slop candidate set reports three consecutive sentences built on one syntactic frame, and its own example is an appositive attribution. Three wire attributions in a row are that frame, which was checked rather than assumed: “Renata Ortiz, a battalion chief at the fire department, said... Tom Whately, an operations director at the freight company, said... Maria Ellison, a deputy marshal at the state office, said...” reports templated-frame with a run of 3. No story in the reference corpus reaches it, because agency copy moves the attribution around - ahead of the quote, behind it, or into a clause of its own - and that movement is the answer to both. The templated-frame finding stands.

This profile asks for more direct quotation, and every span rule in this repository reads a quotation as the writer's own sentence. Over the 35-story reference corpus the built-in and candidate sets report 99 findings, of which 10 sit inside quotation marks, spread across seven rules - not-just, genuinely, performative-honesty, echo-triad, stranded-auxiliary and em-dash among them. Those findings stand as reported. A writer quoting a source accurately is the person best placed to see that the sentence is not theirs, and the alternative, teaching the span rules to skip quoted text, would hand every document a way to hide in quotation marks.

rules.name: Attribution appears less often than this register uses it
rules.description: The rate of the plain attribution verbs said, says and told, counted per 1000 words. This register runs 2 to 14 per 1000 words and the reference median is 6.1. At or below 2 the document is making its claims on its own authority instead of routing them through a person a reader could look up, which is the arrangement wire copy is built on. This rule reports the low edge of that band, and it is a measurement of fit rather than a judgement on the prose: reference material, manuals and analysis sit below it as a matter of course.
rules.suggest: Below the newsroom band (2 to 14 attribution verbs per 1000 words). Put each contested claim in the mouth of a named source and let the verb be said.
rules.measured: floor 2 per 1000; 35 wire stories from the Associated Press and BBC News, 38,067 words, ran 0.0 (min) / 2.4 (p10) / 6.1 (median) / 13.5 (p90) / 17.9 (max), and the edge is p10 rounded down. It reports 4 of those 35 stories and 15 of the 16 documents in this project's local technical corpus that reach the prose gate. Re-measured from the same 35 stories for this revision.
rules.note: Reuters gives the reason for restricting the count to said, says and told: “The verb to say is usually the best, neutral choice in reporting a speech or statement.” The reference rate was measured on 20 Associated Press and 15 BBC News articles taken from their front pages in August 2026, and re-measured for this revision. The pattern is not clean: a story being told counts as attribution here, which is one reason the edge sits at 2 rather than at 0. The near-total miss on the local corpus is the specificity of the register, not a calibration failure - engineering documentation attributes nothing to anybody, which is one of the things that makes it engineering documentation. Selecting this profile is the statement that you want this register, so the fix is an instruction, not a question. If the band is wrong for this document, move it with `tune` in slop.json or drop the profile; do not leave the finding unaddressed on the grounds that the register is a choice.

hit: The ingest service reads each upload into a staging table before anything downstream can see it. Rows land with a batch identifier, a checksum and the time the file arrived. A worker pool then walks the staging table in identifier order and applies three checks to every row. The first check rejects rows whose checksum does not match the bytes on disk. The second rejects rows with a timestamp outside the window the partner agreed to. The third rejects rows that duplicate a key already committed in the previous hour. Rejections are written to a separate table with the reason attached, and the batch continues. Only when every row in a batch has been checked does the worker commit the batch to the main store. A partial batch is never visible, which is the property the reporting team depends on. Commits are serialised per partner, so a slow partner cannot block a fast one. Throughput on the current hardware is about eleven thousand rows a second, measured over a week of production traffic. The bottleneck is the checksum pass, which is single threaded for historical reasons nobody has revisited. Moving it to the worker pool would probably double the number, at the cost of a more complicated failure path. That change has been on the backlog since the spring and keeps losing to work with a deadline. In the meantime the queue drains overnight and the morning report is ready by six, which is the only requirement anyone has written down. Operators watch two numbers: the depth of the staging table and the rejection rate per partner. A rejection rate above two percent for any partner raises a ticket automatically. Most of those tickets close within a day, usually after the partner fixes a date format on their side. The runbook covers the four failure modes seen in the last two years and nothing else. It is short because the system is small, and it stays useful for the same reason.
miss: PORTLAND, Oregon - A fire at a food distribution warehouse on the eastern edge of the city destroyed about four thousand pallets of packaged goods on Tuesday morning, closed two streets until the middle of the afternoon and left a regional grocery supplier without the building it uses to stage deliveries for three states, fire officials said. No one was hurt. Crews reached the warehouse twenty minutes after the first call and spent four hours bringing the fire under control, working around a partial roof collapse that kept them out of the north end of the building. The cause has not been determined. "We had a great deal of fuel in there, the roof came down early, and there was not much room for the crews to work from the inside, so we fought most of it from the yard," said Battalion Chief Renata Ortiz, who led the response and stayed at the scene until the evening. Two streets reopened. The warehouse is leased by Calder Freight, a distributor that supplies about six hundred grocers and employs one hundred and forty people at the site. Its operations director, Tom Whately, put the delay to deliveries at roughly a week. "Every pallet in that building was going out on Thursday, and now it is going nowhere, but every one of our people here will be paid while we sort out where to put the next load," Whately added in an interview at the edge of the cordon. County records show the building was constructed in 1974. The sprinkler system was inspected in March and passed, according to a city fire marshal, who confirmed the paperwork had already gone to the state. The state fire marshal will take over the inquiry on Wednesday and expects to finish it within a month, a spokeswoman for that office said, and the company has until Friday to file its own account of the morning with the county. Insurers have not commented. The site was last valued for tax purposes at 6.2 million dollars. The company was already renting space nearby.

rules.name: Attribution appears more often than this register uses it
rules.description: The same rate read from the other side. This register runs 2 to 14 attribution verbs per 1000 words and the busiest story in the reference corpus reached 17.9. At or above 14 nearly every sentence is handed to a speaker, which is the shape of minutes, a hearing digest or a transcript rather than an account that carries its settled facts in the writer's own sentences. This rule reports the high edge of that band and is a measurement of fit: a record of who said what belongs above it.
rules.suggest: Above the newsroom band (2 to 14 attribution verbs per 1000 words). Let the uncontested facts stand in your own sentences and keep attribution for what is contested, quoted or somebody's judgement.
rules.measured: ceiling 14 per 1000; the same 35 wire stories ran 0.0 (min) / 2.4 (p10) / 6.1 (median) / 13.5 (p90) / 17.9 (max), and the edge is p90 rounded up. It reports 4 of those 35 stories and none of the 16 local documents that reach the prose gate.
rules.note: This edge is corpus-derived and it is the weaker half of the pair. Both guides argue for attribution and neither sets a ceiling, so the number comes from the reference distribution alone, where the four busiest stories run 14.5 to 17.9 per 1000 words. Read it as a description of that corpus rather than as advice. It is here because a floor on its own lets a document drift as far as it likes in the permitted direction, and the documents that do are a recognisable kind: minutes and transcripts run three to five times the wire median. Selecting this profile is the statement that you want this register, so the fix is an instruction, not a question. If the band is wrong for this document, move it with `tune` in slop.json or drop the profile; do not leave the finding unaddressed on the grounds that the register is a choice.

hit: The standards committee met on Tuesday afternoon and worked through nine items in the order they appeared on the circulated agenda. The chair said the minutes of the June meeting had been sent to every member a fortnight earlier and were taken as read. There were no matters arising. The treasurer took the meeting through the quarterly accounts, which had been distributed with the agenda and showed a balance of forty one thousand pounds. He said the audit would be finished before the annual meeting. Two nominations have arrived for the vacant seat on the technical panel, one from the eastern region and one from the north. The secretary said both candidates had confirmed they were willing to serve, and the vote will be held in September. The drafting group has completed the third revision of the fire door schedule, which went out for comment on the tenth of the month. Eleven responses came back within the consultation period and nine of them concern the same clause. The chair of the group said the remaining two responses were expected within the week. The inspection programme is running four weeks behind the schedule agreed in March. The building officer said the delay came from a vacancy in the north team rather than from the volume of work, and interviews are arranged for the first week of the month. Forty seven new members have joined since April. The membership secretary told the meeting that renewals were running slightly ahead of last year and that the printed handbook would go to the printer in November. The next meeting will be held on the second Tuesday of October in the same room. The chair said the papers would go out ten days beforehand, and thanked the room for finishing on time. The meeting closed at four.

rules.name: Passages in direct quotation appear less often than this register carries them
rules.description: The rate of quoted passages of at least fifteen characters on one line, counted per 1000 words. This register runs 2 to 15 per 1000 words and the reference median is 7.7. At or below 2 almost nothing in the document is in somebody else's words, so a reader has only the writer's summary of what was said. This rule reports the low edge of that band and is a measurement of fit rather than a judgement: a specification or a tutorial has nobody to quote and belongs below this edge.
rules.suggest: Below the newsroom band (2 to 15 quoted passages per 1000 words). Carry one or two short direct quotations that push the account forward rather than repeat it.
rules.measured: floor 2 per 1000; the same 35 wire stories, 38,067 words, ran 0.0 (min) / 3.0 (p10) / 7.7 (median) / 14.2 (p90) / 19.9 (max), and the edge sits just under p10. It reports 3 of those 35 stories and 13 of the 16 local documents that reach the prose gate.
rules.note: Reuters: “Direct quotes add colour and strength to your story and they prove you have spoken to someone who knows what happened.” The pattern counts quoted passages rather than quotation marks, because a lone pair of scare quotes around a term of art is not a quotation; raw quotation marks measured 0.0 (median) to 60.1 (max) on the local corpus against 18.4 (median) on the reference corpus, and the paired form separates the two far better. The passage also has to sit on one line. Letting it cross a line break pairs quotation marks from unrelated blocks: on a file of Python source it produced 24.2 quoted passages per 1000 words, above every story in the reference corpus, from string literals in code. The cost of the line rule is that a quotation broken across two source lines is not counted, so a document that hard-wraps its paragraphs reads a little lighter on quotation than it is. On the reference corpus the two forms differ only in the upper half of the distribution: p10, median and maximum are identical and p90 moves from 15.5 to 14.2. Selecting this profile is the statement that you want this register, so the fix is an instruction, not a question. If the band is wrong for this document, move it with `tune` in slop.json or drop the profile; do not leave the finding unaddressed on the grounds that the register is a choice.

rules.name: Passages in direct quotation appear more often than this register carries them
rules.description: The same rate read from the other side. This register runs 2 to 15 quoted passages per 1000 words and the most heavily quoted story in the reference corpus reached 19.9. At or above 15 the document is mostly somebody else's sentences with joins between them, which is a transcript or an interview digest rather than a story that has been reported and arranged. This rule reports the high edge of that band and is a measurement of fit: an oral history or a question-and-answer piece is supposed to sit above it.
rules.suggest: Above the newsroom band (2 to 15 quoted passages per 1000 words). Keep the quotations that carry something a summary cannot, and put the rest in your own sentences with the source named.
rules.measured: ceiling 15 per 1000; the same distribution - 0.0 (min) / 3.0 (p10) / 7.7 (median) / 14.2 (p90) / 19.9 (max) - and the edge is p90 rounded up. It reports 3 of those 35 stories and none of the 16 local documents that reach the prose gate.
rules.note: This edge is corpus-derived. Neither guide sets a ceiling on quotation, so the number comes from the reference distribution alone, where the three most heavily quoted stories run 16.2 to 19.9 per 1000 words. Read it as a description of that corpus. It is here for the same reason as the attribution ceiling: without it the low edge would let a document run to any depth of quotation and report nothing. Selecting this profile is the statement that you want this register, so the fix is an instruction, not a question. If the band is wrong for this document, move it with `tune` in slop.json or drop the profile; do not leave the finding unaddressed on the grounds that the register is a choice.

hit: The transcript below is taken from an hour of recorded conversation with a retired signals engineer who spent thirty years on the coastal chain. It has been trimmed for length and the order of two answers has been swapped, but nothing else has been altered. The station he worked at closed in the middle of the eighties and the buildings were sold four years after that. "We were paid to listen to nothing at all for most of a shift, and the trick was learning to keep your attention on the nothing," he began, settling into the chair by the window. He was posted there in the first week of January, on a road that had not been cleared, in the coldest winter the county had recorded since the war. On the equipment he inherited: "Half of it had been built during the war and the other half had been built to replace the half that failed." He was asked whether the work had been dull, and the question did not land well. "Dull is not the word I would use, because dull suggests you were allowed to stop paying attention," he answered. He described the training at some length, and then summarised it. "They taught us the theory for six weeks and then they taught us the practice for six years." The closure was announced in the spring and the last shift was worked in the November. "We had all known for two years that it was coming, which did not make the last night any easier to work." He paused there for a long moment before finishing the story. "I went back once, about ten years ago, and the road up to it had gone back to grass," he said at the end of the second tape.

rules.name: More coloured attribution verbs than this register carries
rules.description: The rate of attribution verbs that carry a judgement of their own, such as claimed, conceded, revealed, stressed, insisted and pointed out, counted per 1000 words and counted only where the verb is introducing what somebody said: followed by a clause, by a quotation, or by the pronoun that opens one. This register runs below 1.5 per 1000 and the reference median is 0.0. At or above 1.5 the choice of verb is doing editorial work the sentence has not accounted for. This rule reports the high edge of a one-sided band and is a measurement of fit: argument, criticism and review reach for these verbs on purpose.
rules.suggest: Above the newsroom band (under 1.5 coloured attribution verbs per 1000 words). Let most of these go back to said and put the colour in the quotation instead.
rules.measured: ceiling 1.5 per 1000; under this pattern the 35 wire stories ran 0.0 (min) / 0.0 (median) / 1.3 (p90) / 2.4 (max), and the edge is p90 rounded up. It reports 3 of those 35 stories and none of the 16 local documents that reach the prose gate. An earlier form of this rule counted the same verbs in any context and set the edge at 2.5: that form ran 0.0 / 0.0 / 2.4 / 4.6 on the reference corpus and reported one local document whose two matches were a heading reading “Maintains time-parametrization fidelity” and the phrase “a maintained asset”. Of the 20 matches the context-free form found across the local corpus, none was an attribution.
rules.note: The word list is Reuters' own, from two entries in its style guide. Under verbs: “Alleged, claimed or maintained could imply that Reuters does not believe a statement and noted, pointed out, recalled or emphasised suggest that we do.” The same entry names admitted, asserted, affirmed, contended, stressed and suggested as potentially partisan, and the loaded words entry gives the reason: “They all contain an element of judgment by the reporter.” Suggested and argued were left out of the pattern because they are ordinary in technical and academic prose, where they carry no such charge. The clause requirement is there for the same reason: outside a reporting frame every verb on this list is an ordinary verb, and counting them bare measured the vocabulary of a document rather than its attributions. Selecting this profile is the statement that you want this register, so the fix is an instruction, not a question. If the band is wrong for this document, move it with `tune` in slop.json or drop the profile; do not leave the finding unaddressed on the grounds that the register is a choice.

hit: The company unveiled its new platform this week, and the reception has been nothing short of remarkable. Executives boasted that adoption had tripled in a single quarter. The chief executive claimed the product would reshape an entire category within two years, and analysts on the call enthused about margins that had been hard to imagine a year ago. One partner gushed that the integration had taken a single afternoon. Another slammed the incumbent vendors for what he called a decade of standing still. The head of engineering stressed that reliability had never slipped below the published target, and insisted that the platform had run for eleven months without a customer visible outage. A director of product touted the roadmap as the most ambitious the company has attempted. Investors, who had been unusually quiet through a shocking spring, are now openly optimistic. The stock rose sharply on the news. It was, by any measure, a dramatic turn for a business that had been written off by most of the market eighteen months ago. Rivals have been notably silent this week. One competitor conceded privately that the pricing was aggressive. Another maintained that the numbers had been presented selectively. A former employee lamented the loss of the smaller culture that made the early work possible, and hinted that the pace had cost the team more than the leadership admits. Customers, meanwhile, appear thoroughly delighted. Support volumes have fallen for six straight months, which is a genuinely staggering result for a platform of this size. The company plans to publish detailed figures next month, and the market will judge them then, but the mood in the room this week was unmistakably triumphant and, for once, entirely earned. Whatever the figures show, the week has already been called a turning point by people who spent last year calling the company a cautionary tale, and that reversal is itself worth watching. The transformation has been swift, and the coverage has followed it closely.

rules.name: More adjectives and adverbs of judgement than this register carries
rules.description: The rate of adjectives and adverbs that rate what they attach to, such as stunning, devastating, staunch, historic, tragically and obviously, counted per 1000 words. This register runs below 2 per 1000 and the reference median is 0.0. At or above 2 the document is telling its reader how to feel about the facts at about one word in five hundred, which puts the writer's view into sentences that read as reporting. This rule reports the high edge of a one-sided band and is a measurement of fit: a review, an essay or a piece of advocacy is supposed to sit above it.
rules.suggest: Above the newsroom band (under 2 adjectives and adverbs of judgement per 1000 words). Cut the rating word and give the detail or the figure that earned it.
rules.measured: ceiling 2 per 1000; the 35 wire stories ran 0.0 (min) / 0.0 (median) / 1.6 (p90) / 3.3 (max), and the edge sits just above p90. It reports 2 of those 35 stories and none of the 16 local documents that reach the prose gate.
rules.note: The list is Reuters' own examples. hit: The company unveiled its new platform this week, and the reception has been nothing short of remarkable. Executives boasted that adoption had tripled in a single quarter. The chief executive claimed the product would reshape an entire category within two years, and analysts on the call enthused about margins that had been hard to imagine a year ago. One partner gushed that the integration had taken a single afternoon. Another slammed the incumbent vendors for what he called a decade of standing still. The head of engineering stressed that reliability had never slipped below the published target, and insisted that the platform had run for eleven months without a customer visible outage. A director of product touted the roadmap as the most ambitious the company has attempted. Investors, who had been unusually quiet through a shocking spring, are now openly optimistic. The stock rose sharply on the news. It was, by any measure, a dramatic turn for a business that had been written off by most of the market eighteen months ago. Rivals have been notably silent this week. One competitor conceded privately that the pricing was aggressive. Another maintained that the numbers had been presented selectively. A former employee lamented the loss of the smaller culture that made the early work possible, and hinted that the pace had cost the team more than the leadership admits. Customers, meanwhile, appear thoroughly delighted. Support volumes have fallen for six straight months, which is a genuinely staggering result for a platform of this size. The company plans to publish detailed figures next month, and the market will judge them then, but the mood in the room this week was unmistakably triumphant and, for once, entirely earned. Whatever the figures show, the week has already been called a turning point by people who spent last year calling the company a cautionary tale, and that reversal is itself worth watching. The transformation has been swift, and the coverage has followed it closely.
miss: PORTLAND, Oregon - A fire at a food distribution warehouse on the eastern edge of the city destroyed about four thousand pallets of packaged goods on Tuesday morning, closed two streets until the middle of the afternoon and left a regional grocery supplier without the building it uses to stage deliveries for three states, fire officials said. No one was hurt. Crews reached the warehouse twenty minutes after the first call and spent four hours bringing the fire under control, working around a partial roof collapse that kept them out of the north end of the building. The cause has not been determined. "We had a great deal of fuel in there, the roof came down early, and there was not much room for the crews to work from the inside, so we fought most of it from the yard," said Battalion Chief Renata Ortiz, who led the response and stayed at the scene until the evening. Two streets reopened. The warehouse is leased by Calder Freight, a distributor that supplies about six hundred grocers and employs one hundred and forty people at the site. Its operations director, Tom Whately, put the delay to deliveries at roughly a week. "Every pallet in that building was going out on Thursday, and now it is going nowhere, but every one of our people here will be paid while we sort out where to put the next load," Whately added in an interview at the edge of the cordon. County records show the building was constructed in 1974. The sprinkler system was inspected in March and passed, according to a city fire marshal, who confirmed the paperwork had already gone to the state. The state fire marshal will take over the inquiry on Wednesday and expects to finish it within a month, a spokeswoman for that office said, and the company has until Friday to file its own account of the morning with the county. Insurers have not commented. The site was last valued for tax purposes at 6.2 million dollars. The company was already renting space nearby.

rules.name: Sentences longer than this register runs them
rules.description: Sentence endings per 1000 words, which is the reciprocal of mean sentence length: 31 endings is a mean of about 32 words a sentence, and 60 endings is a mean of about 17. This register runs 31 to 60 endings per 1000 words, a mean of 17 to 32 words, and the reference median is 38 endings, or 26 words. At or below 31 the average sentence is carrying more than a reader of a news story is asked to hold at once. This rule reports the long edge of that band and is a measurement of fit rather than a judgement: specifications, contracts and academic prose run longer sentences for good reasons of their own.
rules.suggest: Below the newsroom band (31 to 60 sentence endings per 1000 words, a mean of 17 to 32 words). Put a period halfway along the longest few and check the important elements are still in the first one.
rules.measured: band 31-60 endings per 1000; the 35 wire stories ran 26.1 (min) / 31.0 (p10) / 38.2 (median) / 50.6 (p90) / 60.4 (max), and this edge is p10. It reports 4 of those 35 stories and 5 of the 17 local documents that reach this rule's gate, which is wider than the gate on the other nine.
rules.note: Reuters puts numbers on this directly, for the opening sentence: “If there are more than 25, start to get nervous. If there are more than 30 then get very nervous. By the time you reach 40 it's time to break the sentence in two.” At 50 words, it adds, “you've definitely gone too far.” An edge at 31 endings per 1000 words is a mean of 32 words a sentence, which lands between the second and third of those marks. The band is measured over the whole document rather than the lead, so it is a looser reading of the same guidance. Two limits on the reading. This is the one rule here whose gate is not the engine's default of 60 words a sentence: it runs at 120, the ceiling the shipped economist long-sentences rule uses for the same measurement, because the edge itself is a mean of 32 words and a document at 70 is the case the rule exists for. A review document written one long sentence to a paragraph, averaging 73 words, reports nothing at a ceiling of 60. The cost is named rather than hidden: a file of source code, where the periods are in identifiers and the mean between them runs to 80 words, also reaches this rule and reports, exactly as it does under that shipped rule. The other nine rules in this profile keep the default ceiling, so nothing else here is computed over such a file. The second limit is the ending pattern, which counts the period after a numbered heading, so a document with numbered sections reads a little shorter-sentenced than it is; excluding those endings changed no story in the reference corpus and moved two local documents, one of them across the short edge. A third limit belongs with those two, and it is the largest of the three: the rate divides words by endings, and a heading or a table cell carries words without carrying an ending, so a document built largely of them reads longer-sentenced than its paragraphs are. Four of the five local documents this edge reports are that shape rather than genuinely long-sentenced prose, which is the reason to read the badge as a rate and open the document before believing it. Selecting this profile is the statement that you want this register, so the fix is an instruction, not a question. If the band is wrong for this document, move it with `tune` in slop.json or drop the profile; do not leave the finding unaddressed on the grounds that the register is a choice.

hit: The ingest service reads each upload into a staging table before anything downstream is permitted to observe it, attaching to every row a batch identifier, a checksum and the wall clock time at which the file arrived, so that a worker pool can later walk the table in identifier order. The first validation step rejects any row whose stored checksum fails to match the bytes that were actually written to disk, and it does so without consulting the origin file a second time. The second step rejects any row carrying a timestamp that falls outside the delivery window the partner agreed to in their integration contract, which is the check that catches most of the traffic we end up arguing about. The third step rejects any row that duplicates a key already committed during the preceding hour, with every rejection written to a separate table alongside a machine readable reason so that the batch can continue rather than stalling. Only when every row in a batch has passed or failed each of the three steps does the worker commit that batch to the main store, which means a partially applied batch is never visible to a reader. It is precisely that property, rather than any particular throughput number, that the reporting team has come to depend on over the four years the service has been running in production, and it is the reason nobody has been willing to relax the commit rule. Commits are serialised on a per partner basis so that one slow partner cannot block a fast one, and throughput on the current hardware sits at roughly eleven thousand rows a second averaged over a week of ordinary traffic. The checksum pass is the clear bottleneck, because it remains single threaded for historical reasons that nobody on the current team has ever gone back to examine properly, and it has stayed that way through two hardware refreshes and one migration. Moving that pass into the worker pool would very likely double the figure, at the cost of a considerably more complicated failure path, and the change has sat on the backlog since the spring while losing every planning round to work that arrived with a deadline attached to it.

rules.name: Sentences shorter than this register runs them
rules.description: Sentence endings per 1000 words, the same measurement as the long edge read from the other side: 60 endings is a mean of about 17 words a sentence. This register runs 31 to 60 endings per 1000 words and the reference median is 38, or 26 words. At or above 60 nearly every sentence is one clause, which reads as a list of facts rather than an account that carries a reader from one to the next. This rule reports the short edge of that band and is a measurement of fit: release notes, checklists and reference entries live here on purpose.
rules.suggest: Above the newsroom band (31 to 60 sentence endings per 1000 words, a mean of 17 to 32 words). Join the pairs that belong together and let one longer sentence carry the context.
rules.measured: band 31-60 endings per 1000; the 35 wire stories ran 26.1 (min) / 38.2 (median) / 50.6 (p90) / 60.4 (max), and this edge sits at the corpus maximum rather than at p90. It reports 1 of those 35 stories and 3 of the 16 local documents that reach the prose gate.
rules.note: This edge is corpus-derived, not guide-derived, and it is the weaker of the two. Both guides argue for short sentences and neither sets a floor, so the number comes from the reference corpus alone, where no story went past 60.4 endings per 1000 words. The nearest support is the BBC styleguide on the other half of the same problem: “Staccato sentences are another danger... Each sentence has the same rhythm. It is very difficult for the listener to follow the thread of the narrative when it is delivered in this disjointed way. Vary the length of your sentences.” The edge sits at the corpus maximum rather than at a percentile, so it reports only documents outside everything the reference corpus produced. One artifact to hold against it: the ending pattern counts the period after a numbered heading, so a document with numbered sections reports a little shorter than it reads. Excluding those endings changed none of the 35 reference stories and moved two local documents, one of them from 68.2 to 57.6 and out of this rule. The pattern is left as it stands because it is the one every other set in this repository uses for the same measurement, and the artifact is named here instead. Selecting this profile is the statement that you want this register, so the fix is an instruction, not a question. If the band is wrong for this document, move it with `tune` in slop.json or drop the profile; do not leave the finding unaddressed on the grounds that the register is a choice.

A row that fails that check is rejected, and the second check then reads the timestamp on the row. Rows outside the agreed window are rejected too. The third check looks for a duplicate key. The runbook is short because the system is small, and new operators read the whole of it in an hour. They then shadow a colleague for one shift. After that they carry the pager themselves.

rules.name: Sentences closer to one length than this register keeps them
rules.description: Sentence-length variation, as the coefficient of variation: standard deviation over mean. This register runs 0.57 to 1.25 and the reference median is 0.74. At or below 0.57 the sentences arrive at close to a single length, so the pace never changes and no sentence stands out by being shorter than the ones around it. This rule reports the even edge of that band and is a measurement of fit, not a judgement: procedural and reference writing is often deliberately uniform.

rules.measured: band cv 0.57-1.25; the 35 wire stories ran 0.47 (min) / 0.57 (p10) / 0.74 (median) / 1.23 (p90) / 1.47 (max), and this edge is p10. It reports 3 of those 35 stories and 1 of the 16 local documents that reach the prose gate.
rules.note: BBC News styleguide: “Vary the length of your sentences. You are telling a story, not making a proclamation.” The humanizer-de set already measures the same quantity with a ceiling at 0.4. The two compose rather than collide: above 0.57 neither reports anything, between 0.4 and 0.57 only this band does, and below 0.4 both do and agree. Selecting this profile is the statement that you want this register, so the fix is an instruction, not a question. rules.name: Sentence length swings more than this register keeps it
rules.description: Sentence-length variation, as the coefficient of variation: standard deviation over mean. This register runs 0.57 to 1.25 and the reference median is 0.74. At or above 1.25 the prose alternates between very short sentences and very long ones, which reads as a narrator working the pace rather than an account keeping an even one. This rule reports the uneven edge of that band and is a measurement of fit: essays, columns and fiction earn their effects exactly here.
rules.suggest: Above the newsroom band (variation 0.57 to 1.25). Even out the extremes by breaking up the longest sentences.
rules.measured: band cv 0.57-1.25; the 35 wire stories ran 0.47 (min) / 0.74 (median) / 1.23 (p90) / 1.47 (max), and this edge is p90 rounded up. It reports 3 of those 35 stories and 2 of the 16 local documents that reach the prose gate.
rules.note: This edge is corpus-derived. Neither guide argues against variation, which is why the low edge of this band carries a quotation and this one carries a percentile. That is what removed a file of Python source from this rule's count: split on periods it reported a variation of 1.98, which was a fact about a source file rather than about anybody's prose. hit: The migration went ahead. It began on a Friday evening in October, after eleven weeks of planning meetings that produced a document nobody outside the platform team ever finished reading, and it involved moving four hundred million rows out of a database that had been running since 2014 and into a cluster that had been built, torn down and rebuilt twice over while the plan itself was still being written and rewritten. Nobody slept. Not one of us. The first phase copied the cold partitions, which took nine hours and went exactly as the rehearsal had gone, and the second phase copied the warm partitions, which took four hours longer than the rehearsal because a network policy that nobody had thought to look at was quietly rate limiting the transfer between two availability zones for the whole of that window. We noticed at dawn. The fix took a minute. It was one line. What followed was the part of the weekend that the platform team still talks about, because the cutover itself, the piece that everyone had worried about for three solid months, took eleven seconds from start to finish and produced no errors at all in any of the four dashboards that had been set up specifically to catch them. Then it was over. We went home. Monday was quiet. Nothing broke. The reporting jobs ran on the new cluster without a single change to any of their queries, the nightly export finished forty minutes early for the first time in two years, and the only ticket anyone filed that week was about a dashboard that had been pointing at a decommissioned replica since long before the migration was ever proposed. Nobody had noticed. It still works. Nothing changed. The lesson was cheap. Rehearse the boring parts. Twice.
